title: How people talk about each other: Modeling Generalized Intergroup Bias and Emotion

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating interpersonal group relationship (in-group vs. out-group) by analyzing tweets to predict whether the speaker and the target belong to the same social group, and mapping how interpersonal emotions correlate with these group dynamics.

Using the political party affiliations (Democrat vs. Republican) of US Congress members as 'found supervision' to classify tweets into in-group or out-group communications, and measuring the distribution of negative and positive emotions directed at political allies versus opponents using multi-task neural models (e.g., BERTweet).
